---
title: Text
description: "Free-form strings encoded by a frozen text model."
---

A payment description can carry detail beyond the merchant label, such as
whether the charge is a delivery order. `Text` encodes those free-form strings
with a frozen Hugging Face model. RelFlow learns to combine their representations
with the amount and other fields. It does not fine-tune that encoder or
generate text.

Install the optional text dependency:

```bash
uv add "relflow[text]"
```

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    memo=rf.Text,
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
memo: "North Market delivery order"
disputed: false
```

## Input and options

The Arrow leaf must contain strings. An empty string is valued; a null has a
separate state. Tokenization pads and truncates at `max_length`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | `"google/bert_uncased_L-2_H-128_A-2"` | Hugging Face identifier or local model path. |
| `max_length` | `128` | Positive tokenization length limit. |
| `tokenizer_batch_size` | `4096` | Maximum strings materialized per tokenizer call. |
| `encoder_batch_size` | `32` | Maximum flattened text values per frozen-encoder call. |
| `encoder_pooling` | `"cls"` | `"cls"`, `"mean"`, or `"pooler"`; the last requires `pooler_output`. |
| `cache` | `False` | Reuse pooled frozen-encoder outputs and token rows: `True` keeps every distinct embedding; a positive integer caps retained entries. |
| `store` | `None` | Directory of persistent frozen-encoder vectors shared by every run, split, and field with the same encoder. |
| `resident` | `None` | Accelerator memory in MiB a store may occupy for on-device lookups; `None` automatically budgets CUDA up to a quarter of total device memory, capped at 2 GiB; `0` keeps the store on the host. |
| `objective` | `"l2"` | Embedding reconstruction loss: `"l1"` or `"l2"`. |
| `jitter` | `rf.Jitter()` | Training noise on the pooled frozen embedding before learned projection. |

`cls` and `mean` require `last_hidden_state`. Text fields using the same model
reuse its frozen encoder within the process. Right-padded values are grouped
by length and cropped per encoder batch; left-padded values retain their full
width. `max_length` still controls truncation and tensor storage.

## Repeated text

Repeated descriptions can reuse frozen-encoder outputs across forward passes:

```python
memo = rf.Text(cache=10_000)
```

`cache=False` disables this reuse. `cache=True` retains every distinct tokenized
input encountered; a positive integer retains at most that many entries.
The bounded cache evicts the least frequently reused resident entry, breaking
ties by least recent use. It favors frequent reuse rather than tracking a
global ranking of every description ever seen. Texts that tokenize identically,
including after truncation, can share an entry.

Entries are pristine pooled embeddings stored in CPU memory, separately for
each text field in each process. Encoder device and precision distinguish
entries. The same setting also keeps token rows in a separate least-recently-used
cache: 4,096 rows for `True`, or at most the configured entries for a positive
integer, bounded further by a 64 MiB payload limit and invalidated when tokenizer
settings change. Duplicate strings within a batch are tokenized once either way.
The trainable projection and training jitter still run on every forward pass, so
caching preserves their gradients and fresh noise while avoiding repeated
tokenizer and frozen-encoder work.

Checkpoints retain the `cache` setting but omit cached embeddings and token
rows; a loaded or copied model starts cold. Under DDP, each process builds its
own caches. Use a finite cap when inputs contain many distinct descriptions:
`cache=True` has no embedding limit and can keep growing in host memory.

## Persistent store

Frozen encoder vectors can be reused across tasks, splits, and training
runs when their encoder configuration and token rows match:

```python
model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    memo=rf.Text(store="embeddings/payment-memos"),
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

The directory holds memory-mapped shards named by the encoder configuration,
keyed by token row with the encoder device type and precision. Every split,
run, and field that names the same directory and encoder reads the same
vectors. Missing token rows are encoded and appended, with duplicates within
a batch sharing an encoder result. New vectors wait in memory and are written
as a new shard at the end of every epoch and phase,
or after 65,536 new rows. Shards are added without rewriting existing ones.
Lookups hash whole token rows and binary-search a sorted index, so a batch
resolves without a Python loop over its rows. When the flushed store fits the
`resident` budget, its index and vectors are uploaded to the device once per
index version. Resident hits are answered there without a host round trip;
larger stores answer from the host
index over memory-mapped shards, which the page cache keeps in memory after
first use. The automatic budget applies to CUDA; other devices use the host
index unless given an explicit resident budget. With a store the in-process
embedding `cache` is bypassed; the token-row cache still follows `cache`.

To fill a store ahead of training, provide the application-supplied
`memo_texts` as a string sequence or Arrow column:

```python
model.nodes[rf.Address("memo")].embedder.warm(memo_texts)
```

Run the warmer on the device and under the autocast context training will
use, since precision is part of the key. Nulls are skipped and repeated
strings count once. The trainable projection and training jitter still run on
every forward pass.

## Learning and output

A reconstructing mask trains the decoder against the pristine frozen embedding,
using state loss and the configured content objective on valued targets.
[Jitter](../reference/jitter.qmd) affects only visible continuous inputs,
not strings, token IDs, or target embeddings. Both settings of
`jitter.normalize` act at the same pooled-embedding boundary.

Text has no decoded public state/content payload. `embed=True` exports a
contextual relflow embedding, distinct from the frozen encoder output; see
[shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options).
Use [Vector](vector.qmd) when the source already supplies an embedding.

## External model assets

The first use of a remote model identifier may download tokenizer and encoder
assets. relflow checkpoints save the request and learned relflow weights,
but do not bundle those external assets. Every loading or serving process
must be able to resolve the same identifier or local path. For reproducible
deployment, prepare a pinned encoder directory and ship it with the artifact.
